title: Order cancellation refinement
summary: Clarify cancellation eligibility and its race with asynchronous shipping.

input_assessment.summary: The source is informal and omits actor, exact state eligibility, failure behavior, and concurrency semantics.

exploration.stop_reason: The public state model and asynchronous transition are sufficient to demonstrate the material ambiguity.

sources.label: Cancellation request
sources.original_text: precisa colocar um botão para cancelar pedido caso ainda não tenha saído

sources.label: Shipping worker note
sources.original_text: O worker de expedição envia pedidos pagos de forma assíncrona.

needs.title: Cancel an eligible order
needs.statement: A customer needs to cancel an order while it remains eligible before shipment.

needs.title: Advance shipping asynchronously
needs.statement: The shipping worker advances paid orders through fulfillment states.
acceptance_signals: The worker advances the persisted order state

evidence.detail: The source says the order can be cancelled when it has not left yet, without defining exact states.
The supplied note states that a worker changes shipping state asynchronously.

evidence.summary: Order state lifecycle and worker transition
evidence.detail: The public state list includes CREATED, PAID, PACKING, and SHIPPED; the worker can transition PACKING to SHIPPED.

relationships.title: Cancellation competes with shipping
relationships.detail: Cancellation and shipping can attempt competing transitions on the same order.

questions.question: Is PACKING still eligible for cancellation, and which transition wins a race?
questions.why_material: The answer changes observable eligibility, persistence semantics, and conflict behavior.

constraints.statement: The existing persisted state lifecycle includes PACKING and SHIPPED.

findings.title: Cancellation eligibility and transition race are undefined
findings.problem: Before shipment does not define whether PACKING is cancellable or how cancellation races with the asynchronous shipping transition.
findings.why_it_matters: A read-then-write implementation can cancel an order after shipping has already won, producing contradictory state or customer feedback.
findings.impact: Observable order behavior and persisted state consistency remain undefined.

final_assessment.rationale: The source describes one coherent cancellation capability, but its state and concurrency behavior are not ready for documentary authority.

handoff.reason: FND-001 remains an open BLOCKING finding.
